hints: Look closely at compound X and name the two different carbonyl groups present.
Remember that one is an aldehyde, $\text{-CHO}$, and the other is a ketone, $\text{CH}_3\text{C=O}$, so think about how their oxidation behaviour differs.
Ask yourself which reagent is a selective oxidising agent that oxidises aldehydes but leaves ketones unchanged, while the other reagents add to or reduce all $\text{C=O}$ groups.
walkthrough:
**Identify the two functional groups**

Great start, let's read the structure. Compound X is $\text{CH}_3\text{COCHO}$.

On the left you have a ketone, $\text{CH}_3\text{C=O}$, and on the right you have an aldehyde, $\text{-CHO}$. So this is a keto-aldehyde.

**Recall what each reagent does to carbonyls**

Now think like a chemist. 2,4-DNPH gives an orange precipitate with any aldehyde or ketone. $\text{HCN}$ adds across any $\text{C=O}$ to form a cyanohydrin. $\text{NaBH}_4$ reduces any $\text{C=O}$ to an alcohol.

$$\text{R}_2\text{C=O} + \text{HCN} \rightarrow \text{R}_2\text{C(OH)CN}$$
$$\text{C=O} + 2[\text{H}] \xrightarrow{\text{NaBH}_4} \text{CH-OH}$$

**Spot the selective reagent**

Acidified potassium dichromate(VI) is a strong but selective oxidising agent. It oxidises an aldehyde to a carboxylic acid, but it cannot oxidise a ketone because there is no hydrogen on the carbonyl carbon to remove.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{COCHO} + [\text{O}] \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COCOOH}$$

Only the $\text{-CHO}$ group reacts, the ketone stays unchanged. That is the unique one-group reaction.

options.A: Correct. Acidified $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ oxidises aldehydes to carboxylic acids but does not oxidise ketones. Here only the $\text{-CHO}$ group is oxidised to $\text{-COOH}$, giving pyruvic acid, while the $\text{CH}_3\text{C=O}$ ketone is untouched.
options.B: False. 2,4-DNPH reagent reacts with the $\text{C=O}$ group of both aldehydes and ketones to give an orange precipitate. Since X has two $\text{C=O}$ groups, both would react, not just one.
options.C: False. Hydrogen cyanide undergoes nucleophilic addition to all carbonyl groups. Both the aldehyde and the ketone in X would form cyanohydrins, so two groups react.
options.D: False. $\text{NaBH}_4$ is a reducing agent that reduces both aldehydes to primary alcohols and ketones to secondary alcohols. Both $\text{C=O}$ groups in X would be reduced, so it is not selective.
